dedupe_keys.name: global water watch satellite surface water area time series for 71 208 reservoirs and lakes 1985 2026 with archive

description: Global Water Watch (GWW) publishes near-real-time surface water area time series for small and medium-sized reservoirs and lakes worldwide, derived from Landsat and Sentinel-2 imagery processed on Google Earth Engine. It was developed by Deltares, WWF and the World Resources Institute with support from Google.org, the Water, Peace and Security Partnership and ESA, following the method of Donchyts and co-authors in Scientific Reports (2022). Coverage: 71,208 reservoirs and lakes worldwide, monthly from January 1985 to 2026, with about 45 million individual satellite observations and reservoir outlines. Format and access: an interactive viewer and API on globalwaterwatch.earth, and a September 2026 preservation archive of the full API content as one NetCDF4 CF-1.10 file on GitHub with a Zenodo DOI, holding filtered monthly areas in square metres, raw per-overpass areas with timestamps, names where recorded, a retrieval flag and outlines; free. Licence: CC-BY-4.0 for the time series; the reservoir outlines are OpenStreetMap-derived and stay under ODbL 1.0. Caveats: the site says GWW will be unavailable from November 2026 because the platform became outdated for lack of funding and team stability, so the live API will go offline; most reservoirs have no name, some downloads were abandoned after retries, and areas are affected by cloud and shadow despite filtering. Simulation uses: reservoir storage dynamics for water supply capacity planning, drought and flood hazard exposure and climate adaptation of hydropower and water systems. Related records: GRanD (data-grand-global-reservoir-and-dam-database) and the Global Dam Watch database (data-global-dam-watch-database) give dam attributes.
